title: onboard.test.js full-suite hangs/OOMs; provision_wifi step-index tests are stale
description:
Discovered while implementing ADR-005 (mothership-level WiFi settings).

1. Running the full dashboard/js/onboard.test.js suite via jest hangs indefinitely
   (confirmed with --max-old-space-size=16000, still not done after 180s) or OOMs
   at lower heap limits. Reproduces on pristine origin/main (commit 8ad051f) with
   zero code changes -- verified via git stash. Root cause not yet investigated;
   suspect a leaked timer/interval (calibrateTimer, pollTimer, or WebSocket mock)
   not cleared between tests outside the "Wizard state transitions" describe block
   (only that block has an explicit afterEach(() => SpaxelOnboard.close())).
   Individual describe blocks run fine in isolation via `jest -t "<pattern>"`.

2. Three pre-existing tests reference stale step indices from before STEPS was
   reordered (WiFi moved before Flash): "provision_wifi step renders form with
   WiFi fields", "provision_wifi shows error for empty SSID" (both prime
   currentStepIndex: 3, which is now flash_firmware, not provision_wifi -- landing
   on connect_device instead due to the flash-step port-reset redirect), and
   "restores state at step 3 (provision_wifi)" in the
   testRestoreAtStep(3, 'provision_wifi') table. All three fail identically on
   pristine origin/main -- confirmed via git stash comparison. Correct index for
   provision_wifi is 2, not 3.

Neither is caused by the ADR-005 change (bf-49kpf/bf-64sf9/bf-1yrdd/bf-415c8).
Both reproduce on unmodified origin/main. Not fixed as part of that work to keep
the diff scoped; flagging so it isn't lost.

title: Move WiFi credentials to mothership-level config (SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID/PASSWORD), stop asking per-device

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Implements ADR-005 (docs/plan/plan.md). Full rationale and design there; summary:

Every ESP32-S3 node is presumed to join the same fleet WiFi network, but wifi_ssid/wifi_pass are currently collected fresh from the user on every single onboarding (dashboard 'Configure WiFi' step -> POST /api/provision request body -> echoed into the provisioning payload). The mothership never stores them. This is what turned today's bench onboarding into a multi-hour ordeal: typing/pasting the real network password into a captive-portal form on every single flash attempt, with no way to avoid it.

Scope:
1. Add SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID / SPAXEL_WIFI_PASSWORD env vars (mothership).
2. POST /api/provision: default wifi_ssid/wifi_pass from that config; keep request-body values as an explicit per-node override (never silently drop the override capability -- some node may legitimately need a different network).
3. Return an error (not a silently-broken provisioning payload) if neither the mothership config nor the request body supplies credentials.
4. Dashboard onboarding wizard: skip the WiFi step entirely when the mothership reports SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID is configured; keep it as an 'Advanced: use a different network' override.
5. Dashboard's captive-portal recovery screen: display the stored credentials in copy-paste-ready form (it cannot submit them automatically -- the browser has no route to the mothership while joined to the device's temporary spaxel-XXXX AP -- see ADR-005 Alternatives Considered for why serial+captive-portal both still need to exist as separate paths).

No firmware changes needed -- this is purely mothership + dashboard, the NVS schema and on-device provisioning protocol are unaffected.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Design revised 2026-08-03 (see plan.md ADR-005, updated). The original write-up used SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID/PASSWORD env vars as the primary mechanism -- wrong call, corrected on review: this is a value a non-technical end user sets up and occasionally changes (router rotation, network move), not infrastructure-operator config chosen once at deploy time like SPAXEL_NTP_SERVER.

Revised scope:
1. New NetworkSettingsHandler (mothership/internal/api/), GET/PUT /api/settings/network, following NotificationSettingsHandler (internal/api/notification_settings.go) as the template exactly -- same shared settings table, typed request/response structs, same RegisterRoutes pattern.
2. Dashboard: new Settings > Network section using that API -- one-time setup, editable anytime, no redeploy.
3. POST /api/provision: default wifi_ssid/wifi_pass from the stored network setting; request-body values still override per-node when supplied; error (not silent broken payload) if neither source has credentials.
4. Onboarding wizard: skip the WiFi step when the setting exists; keep as 'Advanced: use a different network' override.
5. Captive-portal recovery screen: display the stored credentials in copy-paste-ready form (still can't submit automatically -- browser has no route to mothership while joined to the device's temporary AP).
6. SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID/PASSWORD env vars: optional first-boot-only seed for scripted deployments. Must NOT re-apply on later boots or clobber a since-changed DB value -- needs explicit test coverage for that specific case.

Still no firmware changes needed.
